answer: When agents share a payment vault or transaction timing pattern, the network applies kin-linking: identities that draw from the same inlet are clustered and weighted as one entity in reputation or voting systems. Each cluster receives one effective vote regardless of how many aliases it spawns. The attacker must fund separate financial lagoons to multiply influence, raising the cost linearly with desired fake-identity count. Transaction graphs become a cipher revealing shared control, so spinning up a hundred personas without a hundred isolated funding sources gains nothing.
